if-eth::D.attackDescription: Attacker applies excessive electrical input or flooding signals to the interface causing it to fail
if-eth::D.causeDescription: Interface has no protection against electrical stress or signal flooding — it can be disabled by physical or signal attack
if-eth::D.threatDescription: Interface denial of service — attacker renders the interface unavailable

if-eth::E.attackDescription: Attacker exploits the interface to run privileged commands and bypass access controls, or uploads unsigned malicious firmware that disables security controls or installs a persistent backdoor
if-eth::E.causeDescription: Interface exposes privileged functions without sufficient authentication and accepts firmware updates without signature verification
if-eth::E.threatDescription: Interface privilege escalation — attacker uses the interface to gain elevated access or inject unauthorized firmware

if-eth::I.attackDescription: Attacker attaches monitoring equipment to the physical interface and captures transmitted data
if-eth::I.causeDescription: Physical interface transmits data without encryption — signals are readable with basic test equipment
if-eth::I.threatDescription: Interface eavesdropping — attacker intercepts data on the physical interface

if-eth::R.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the physical interface and denies having accessed it because no log record exists
if-eth::R.causeDescription: No logging of physical interface connections — who connected and when is unknown
if-eth::R.threatDescription: Interface access repudiation — physical interface access cannot be attributed

if-eth::S.attackDescription: Attacker connects a rogue device to the interface and impersonates a legitimate system, gaining unauthorized access
if-eth::S.causeDescription: No hardware authentication on the interface — any device connecting is trusted without verification
if-eth::S.threatDescription: Interface identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate device on the interface

if-eth::T.attackDescription: Attacker modifies the interface hardware or firmware to intercept, inject, or block communications
if-eth::T.causeDescription: Interface lacks tamper detection and physical protection — unauthorized modification is possible without detection
if-eth::T.threatDescription: Interface tampering — attacker physically or logically tampers with the interface

el::if-jtag::D.attackDescription: Attacker applies excessive electrical input or flooding signals to the interface causing it to fail
el::if-jtag::D.causeDescription: Interface has no protection against electrical stress or signal flooding — it can be disabled by physical or signal attack
el::if-jtag::D.threatDescription: Interface denial of service — attacker renders the interface unavailable

el::if-jtag::R.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the physical interface and denies having accessed it because no log record exists
el::if-jtag::R.causeDescription: No logging of physical interface connections — who connected and when is unknown
el::if-jtag::R.threatDescription: Interface access repudiation — physical interface access cannot be attributed

el::if-jtag::S.attackDescription: Attacker connects a rogue device to the interface and impersonates a legitimate system, gaining unauthorized access
el::if-jtag::S.causeDescription: No hardware authentication on the interface — any device connecting is trusted without verification
el::if-jtag::S.threatDescription: Interface identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate device on the interface

el::if-touch::D.attackDescription: Attacker floods or jams the wireless channel (RF interference, connection/association flooding) causing the interface to drop or become unresponsive
el::if-touch::D.causeDescription: Wireless interface has no protection against signal flooding or jamming and no redundant path — it can be disabled by overwhelming the channel
el::if-touch::D.threatDescription: Interface denial of service (wireless) — attacker jams or floods the wireless interface to render it unavailable

el::if-touch::E.attackDescription: Attacker exploits the interface to run privileged commands and bypass access controls, or uploads unsigned malicious firmware that disables security controls or installs a persistent backdoor
el::if-touch::E.causeDescription: Interface exposes privileged functions without sufficient authentication and accepts firmware updates without signature verification
el::if-touch::E.threatDescription: Interface privilege escalation — attacker uses the interface to gain elevated access or inject unauthorized firmware

el::if-touch::R.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the physical interface and denies having accessed it because no log record exists
el::if-touch::R.causeDescription: No logging of physical interface connections — who connected and when is unknown
el::if-touch::R.threatDescription: Interface access repudiation — physical interface access cannot be attributed

el::if-touch::S.attackDescription: Attacker connects a rogue device to the interface and impersonates a legitimate system, gaining unauthorized access
el::if-touch::S.causeDescription: No hardware authentication on the interface — any device connecting is trusted without verification
el::if-touch::S.threatDescription: Interface identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate device on the interface

el::if-touch::T.attackDescription: Attacker modifies the interface hardware or firmware to intercept, inject, or block communications
el::if-touch::T.causeDescription: Interface lacks tamper detection and physical protection — unauthorized modification is possible without detection
el::if-touch::T.threatDescription: Interface tampering — attacker physically or logically tampers with the interface

el::if-usb::D.attackDescription: Attacker applies excessive electrical input or flooding signals to the interface causing it to fail
el::if-usb::D.causeDescription: Interface has no protection against electrical stress or signal flooding — it can be disabled by physical or signal attack
el::if-usb::D.threatDescription: Interface denial of service — attacker renders the interface unavailable

el::if-usb::E.attackDescription: Attacker exploits the interface to run privileged commands and bypass access controls, or uploads unsigned malicious firmware that disables security controls or installs a persistent backdoor
el::if-usb::E.causeDescription: Interface exposes privileged functions without sufficient authentication and accepts firmware updates without signature verification
el::if-usb::E.threatDescription: Interface privilege escalation — attacker uses the interface to gain elevated access or inject unauthorized firmware

el::if-usb::I.attackDescription: Attacker attaches monitoring equipment to the physical interface and captures transmitted data
el::if-usb::I.causeDescription: Physical interface transmits data without encryption — signals are readable with basic test equipment
el::if-usb::I.threatDescription: Interface eavesdropping — attacker intercepts data on the physical interface

el::if-usb::R.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the physical interface and denies having accessed it because no log record exists
el::if-usb::R.causeDescription: No logging of physical interface connections — who connected and when is unknown
el::if-usb::R.threatDescription: Interface access repudiation — physical interface access cannot be attributed

el::if-usb::S.attackDescription: Attacker connects a rogue device to the interface and impersonates a legitimate system, gaining unauthorized access
el::if-usb::S.causeDescription: No hardware authentication on the interface — any device connecting is trusted without verification
el::if-usb::S.threatDescription: Interface identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate device on the interface

el::if-usb::T.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the maintenance interface outside any scheduled window
el::if-usb::T.causeDescription: Interface declared maintenance-only but no policy enforcement disables it outside windows
el::if-usb::T.threatDescription: Maintenance interface accessible outside maintenance window — unauthorized privileged access at any time

el::pb-cab::D.attackDescription: Attacker physically damages the device or cuts power, causing immediate loss of availability
el::pb-cab::D.causeDescription: No physical protection or anchoring — device can be damaged, unplugged, or destroyed
el::pb-cab::D.threatDescription: Physical destruction or power disruption — device rendered unavailable by physical attack

el::pb-cab::E.attackDescription: Attacker opens the physical boundary and connects to internal debug interface, bypassing all software authentication
el::pb-cab::E.causeDescription: Physical access to device interior grants debug/hardware access — logical security can be bypassed
el::pb-cab::E.threatDescription: Physical privilege escalation — attacker gains elevated system access via physical boundary breach

el::pb-cab::I.attackDescription: Attacker inserts removable media and copies sensitive files or cryptographic material
el::pb-cab::I.causeDescription: Removable media port accessible — no data loss prevention mechanism
el::pb-cab::I.threatDescription: Data exfiltration via removable media — sensitive data copied out of device

el::pb-cab::S.attackDescription: Attacker impersonates an authorized person (e.g. maintenance technician) to gain physical access to the boundary interior
el::pb-cab::S.causeDescription: Physical access control relies on single-factor authentication — no second factor prevents impersonation
el::pb-cab::S.threatDescription: Physical boundary identity spoofing — attacker impersonates authorized personnel to gain physical access

el::pb-cab::T.attackDescription: Attacker inserts a USB drive containing malware or uses it to exfiltrate sensitive data
el::pb-cab::T.causeDescription: Removable media port is physically accessible — no software or physical blocking
el::pb-cab::T.threatDescription: Removable media insertion — unauthorized data exfiltration or malware injection via physical media
